title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
pattern: Preorder gives the root, inorder splits left / right
statement: `preorder` and `inorder` are the preorder and inorder traversals of the same binary tree (all values are different). Rebuild the tree and return its root.

example.why: 3 is the root; 9 is everything to its left; 20 (with children 15 and 7) is its right subtree.

idea: **Preorder** visits a node *before* its subtrees, so its first value is always the root.

**Inorder** visits the left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree. So once the root is located in `inorder`, everything left of it is the left subtree and everything right of it is the right subtree.

Apply the same step to each side. Roots are taken from `preorder` one after another, which works because preorder lists the entire left subtree before the right one. A value → index map finds each root in `inorder` instantly, and a pair of indexes describes a part of `inorder` without copying it.

complexity.timeWhy: Every value becomes a node exactly once, and finding it in `inorder` is a single map lookup.
complexity.spaceWhy: The value → index map, plus a recursion as deep as the tree's height.

steps.text: Our example: **`preorder = [3,9,20,15,7], inorder = [9,3,15,20,7]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
